podcast.title: A rumour from a ladder

hosts.Leyla: lives in Baku and loves a good plan
hosts.Sam: grew up in Manchester and once travelled with no plan at all

before.predict: Do you believe everything you read? Guess: what is the big rumour in Sam and Leyla's street?

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is news and rumours. And there's a big rumour in our street.
Oh, I know. Mr Aliyev is selling his house.
That is what everyone says! The woman at the bakery told me, and the taxi driver told her.
In two days it was the talk of the town. And do you know what's really happening?
No, what?
He's painting it. That's all. Somebody saw the workers and the ladders.
[laugh] So the rumour started with a ladder!
That's how gossip works. It spreads faster than the truth.
My mum is the same with the internet. She reads a headline and calls me straight away.
My grandmother too! She sends messages to the family group: "Lemon water cures everything!"
And who says that?
Exactly my question: what's the source? Usually, nobody knows.
I have a rule: if it's very shocking, I take it with a pinch of salt.
Good rule. And I read the same story in two or three places. Some news sites are very biased.
True. Each one tells you only its half of the story.
But some news is real. Who told you about your sister's engagement?
My mum! She called at six in the morning to break the news. She couldn't wait.
[chuckle] That's the best kind of news.
And it was true — I checked with my sister. [laugh]
Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: where do you get your news — and how do you know if it's true?
And tell your partner the funniest rumour you ever heard. See you next time!
Bye for now!
